title: The corruption of lineages through appetite
english: He hates misfortune. And because of this, it comes to pass that the house of the fasting person has angels as guardians, protectors, and attendants, while the one indulging in pleasures during the forty days has demons as household members, and lovers and lustful ones of blood, and attendants of drunkenness. For even regarding the spirits, whether holy or unclean, each one approaches its own kind and friends, just as it can be seen among birds.

For a dove indeed loves the pure places and turns itself toward the clearings, sowing seed for itself and its young; and the berry sits sweetly upon the tree leaves, producing something sweet and thin. But the gluttonous raven sits near the butcher shops, heavy and unpleasant, descending upon those who are slaughtering meat.

Therefore, let us love self-control, so that we may be loved by angels, and let us hate unrestrained luxury, so that we may not cast ourselves into fellowship with demons along with it. No one living in luxury became diligent, nor is one idling in prayers a disciple of virtue, nor is a lover of pleasure a saint, nor is one living fleshly a companion of the kingdom.

Come into your memory toward the beginning of our race and you will find the experience of those of whom we are witnesses. For a law of fasting would not have been set for us if the law of first self-control had not been surpassed; nor would the stomach have been named an intruder, if the pretext of pleasure had not introduced sin.

There was no need for the plow, nor for oxen to plow, nor for the cutting of the furrow, nor indeed for the sowing of seed and the watering, nor for the cycle of seasons, nor for the thickening of winter and the loosening of summer, nor for all this cyclical toil, if we had not decided upon the cycle of labors for the sake of an easy, immediate enjoyment of this [life]; but we intended a different state of life from the one seen, which we again hope to attain when we put on the impassible life through the resurrection.

For this is the blessing of God's condescension toward us, so that we might restore our worth toward the former [state]; which, having taken hold of philanthropically, we did not preserve, feeling the grace sensitively. Let us therefore be brightened at the coming fast; an icon of the coming life, a mimic of the incorruptible conduct. There are neither drinking parties nor pleasures...

Leave the first man, and count those after him as well. Why did it make the righteous Noah act shamefully, being stripped of his members which law should cover, and prepare to mock the impious Ham through the drunkenness of his father (Gen 9:20-27), so that two evils might come from one fault? For one drunkenness stripped both the father of the good covering and the son of liberty.

But when I turn again to the children of Eli the priest and to that history (1 Sam 2), I find a cluster of misfortunes connected to one another from a single source, that of the belly and the penis. For they, having made the priesthood of the father a starting point for pleasure and enjoyment, defiled the sacrifices and went toward the belly before God of the priests. And fornication followed, the sister of the sin of luxury, and to all these, the judgment from God brings a strict and sudden sentence.

For an enemy nation marched against Jerusalem because of them. And so that the word might cut short a multitude of gloomy narratives, the unrestrained youths fell in battle, the mother endangered with the sinners, and the ark of God was taken captive by the enemies, and the old priest died at the messages of evils, and so much of our evil was brought upon the city through the pleasure of the throat.

Therefore, let us all fast; especially those who are members of the priests, and more so as having the teaching of self-control and the philosophical commands from the table as a co-dweller. For it is absurd for the children of money-changers to be silver-knowers, and the members of the coppersmiths to be near the fire and the bellows, but for the members of the priests, whether relatives or otherwise, to neglect the object of life which the master and lord of the hearth was permitted to live. He was most harmed through the belly, even the elder son of Isaac (Gen 25). For being a hunter by profession and once, after a great run to the house, returning hungry, he took in the food that was before him, and he gave the firstborns to the lentil-eater (Gen 25:30-34); from there, moreover, he also snatched away the paternal blessing, and thus, being made a stranger little by little, he lost virtue and the patriarchal glory of God.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Soul and the Body
english: He lost even Israel through their lifestyle, becoming himself a barbarian and a stranger, and begetting a people like him. This disease led even the people of the old covenant into transgression of the divine and holy laws. For while Moses was occupied with the leisure of the giving of the law, the people, being distracted, turned toward luxury and dancing; the devil dragged them, as they were slipping and trampling the order of life toward impiety. From there, the demon-possessed skill of calf-making, Aaron sharing in the defilement and the corruption of the law, the smashing of the tablets, and Moses' second ascent to the mountain—all these things, which the history mocks with full detail, had their beginning and cause in immoderate eating.

I wish to set before you another account, second in time to what was said before, but equal in practice. King Saul was preparing and leading the war with much care; he forbade the people to take food on that day, sealing the judgment with an oath, and death was the penalty to the one who disobeyed. But while the whole army obediently received the command, only the king's son Jonathan stumbled, being overcome by the honey, and he dared to taste the scepter of sweetness by rushing toward the lords. Danger came near, unless the whole multitude, acting in concert with the impulse of their father and king, decided to turn the threat into action.

Regarding what has been said, it is possible to collect ten thousand such things from the Scriptures to see clearly that self-control is good, and conversely, the unrestrained enjoyment of drink and food is harmful. Fasting is the companion of the saints; fasting is the leader of every good work. And just as craftsmen do not perform their arts without tools, so also the diligent, even when helping with spiritual gifts, have never performed any of the wonders and marvels without self-control. Fasting Elijah raised the dead and gave them life; fasting Moses saw God; fasting Daniel mastered the sorcery and error of the Assyrians; fasting the Lord withstood the temptations of the devil; and fasting the...

The apostles performed prayers for important matters; the Ninevites through fasting overcame the threat of death (Jonah 3:5-10). This [prayer] is an intercessor toward God, worthy of reverence, and a reliable embassy that quickly covers itself with shame for whatever supplication it brings to God.

Therefore, let every pious man, who loves God more than pleasure, approach the days of self-control with joy and good cheer. For no one who is merely a scavenger is a noble combatant at the beginning of the contests.

Do not become sullen like a child being dragged to school; do not grumble about the purity of the days; do not seek the end of the week like the arrival of spring after a bitter winter; do not long for the Sabbath for the sake of feasting like a Jew (Exodus 16); do not count the days of the forty [days] like a lazy laborer waiting for the end of his agreed-upon wage; do not grieve because from the first hour your house is not smoking, nor has the cook stood by the fire.

Grant something also to the soul, not everything to the body. The former nourishes by the withholding of food, the latter by the abundance. But since the two are joined to one another, and those which are much separated by nature are seated together by the providence and art of the Creator, let us deliberate so that both might happen, each not being deprived of what is appropriate. You, O man, were composed of the two, and I am entirely silent as to the fact that the soul is much more preferable and it was fitting that it should receive the greater share of favor.

But judge between both as a rational and discerning man. Consider a little, and if you wish, I will make the argument for the soul as if to a faithful woman, providing support regarding those things of which she says she is being treated unjustly and being cast down. This, then, is sacred and incorporeal, immortal and incorruptible, having its kinship not toward earth and these things, but toward God. Being pure, she rejoices with the pure, and having an incorporeal origin, she flees from material substances.

However, since the vessel formed from the earth was commanded to be managed, as an obedient handmaid to the Lord, she sits upon the clay and is subject to the guarding and the providence over it, until the command comes allowing the separation. This [abstinence] from food, which gives life to the body, is necessary; but for the organ of the earth, the enjoyment of food is necessary. He seeks nothing...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Virtue of Temperance and the Example of Barbarians
english: Even more so as a superior. 'Divide to me, he says, the time of the year; give the six months for enjoyment to the one being governed and the remaining to the governor.' The request is just, and no judge is so fond of wisdom, being a heterodox judge, as not to vote in favor of those things being said. But I will even do an excess; I do not hold to equality. I descend with the weakness of the body. I leave ten months to the body and a little more. Let the fortieth be granted to me, unpolluted, so that I might be slightly freed from the filth, the mud, having been cooled by self-control. These things, O Christians, are both just and irrefutable, even if God judges and even if man judges. And you also, O judge, vote in my favor, for the time has arrived when the soul is disputing against the body. Therefore, take away from me, O Christian, the sensuality as if it were childish. You are a man; do not think the things of infants. If he does not receive that of honey, he wails; if you do not crave meat or wine, he falls away, tears himself apart, and knocks down everyone for more, while lamenting. I redden at the descent of the gluttons, so that they might mourn the fasting; they are constantly gaping, they are slightly overcome, they pass away again, they sleep by necessity. In insensibility they strive to pass the days, they are weary of the sun toward the setting as it grows late. They approach the days as longer than the habit. Moreover, they wash their aching stomachs and the tensions of the spirits and the heaviness of the head and the dizziness of the state. Even if these things are of surfeit, they are not the characteristics of fasting. They come to the solemn table joylessly, they grumble about the vegetables, they revile the legumes as if they were an addition added to creation; for the lovers of pleasure become also blowhards against the appearances of self-control. 14.10.5 They draw water without breath as if they had received a tasteless medicine from physicians to drink. And many also act wise regarding wine, persuading their pleasure with illicit concoctions. And others immediately attend to the need for vegetables and become various sophists of enjoyment. But this is very habitual and senseless. 14.10.6 For self-control is a struggle of the self-governing and of the free mind, m—
The text ends abruptly with a fragment: 'μ' (m—).

For a slave-like craft, seeking what is set before it, does not work it as it should, but fashions it in a slavish way. You demand a reward for those things according to which you live by the law of virtue. But a reward is promised to honest workers, not to evildoers.

Do not corrupt the fast, so that you do not suffer the things of the charcoal-burners. For if those, mixing water with wine, are punished, how will you, by introducing your sophisticated pleasures into the strictness of the fast, pass through unpunished? Do not imitate formed weaknesses; do not deceive yourself regarding the forty days as if it were a disease-maker, for on the contrary, it is a maker of health. Do not make pretexts for sins while working with men driven by lust.

Because of bad habit, self-control is considered an enemy to you; it is not, however, naturally offensive. All barbarians are a proof of this word, those who neither plant vines nor drink wine, but instead take for themselves by habit an uncultivated drink, water, and they are known to be brave and excellent in wars and they hold sway over the many, as is fitting, those who are drunk while they are sober.

But bodies to them are light and vigorous, and such people are quick to mount a horse, and are skillful and bold and accurate toward archery. And they are capable of finding safety amidst the tumult and finding a course in destitute places. Therefore, do not accuse water as being an emollient, and do not say that those using it are weak; for experience will expose your slander.

What do I say about wine? The Scythian nomads, those who dwell by the Bosporus and those who are stationed by the Rhine river, are indeed homeless and unstanding. But they live from skins and hides and from the hanging veils, making for themselves a covering.

But they do not know a plow, nor do they turn the soil; therefore they also do not bring bread. For how could those who have not learned agriculture regarding grain and the subsequent seeds be expected to? Nevertheless, living without bread and wine, they are brave and worthy of fighting war against all nations, and they hold sway over and excel the many; and neither bread nor wine being absent from them harmed them, but the ancestral habit became nature to men.
Why then did the word mention these things? In order that...
